assessments.source_element: sketching the cake design and deciding flavors for the first layer
assessments.target_element: planning phase (defining objectives, alternatives, and approach)
assessments.rationale: Both activities involve defining overall goals and selecting options before any concrete work begins; the analogy captures the intent of a planning stage.

assessments.source_element: taste‑testing a small batch of the first layer to see if the flavor works and if it bakes evenly
assessments.target_element: risk analysis (identifying and evaluating risks before full development)
assessments.rationale: A taste test is a limited, sensory probe that mirrors the idea of probing for problems, but software risk analysis covers many dimensions (schedule, cost, technical debt) that a simple flavor test cannot represent fully.

assessments.source_element: baking the first layer fully and evaluating how it turned out
assessments.target_element: engineering (development) followed by evaluation (testing and validation)
assessments.rationale: Fully baking the layer corresponds to constructing a software increment, and the subsequent evaluation mirrors testing/validation; the mapping preserves the sequence and purpose of these phases.

assessments.source_element: repeating the design‑test‑bake‑evaluate cycle for each subsequent layer, adjusting based on prior results
assessments.target_element: iterative cycles for each increment, refining the software based on previous risk assessment and evaluation
assessments.rationale: The repeated cycle captures the core iterative, risk‑driven nature of the spiral model, with each loop building on lessons from the previous one.

structural_issues: Taste‑testing captures only a narrow subset of software risks, making the risk‑analysis mapping a logical stretch.
The cake analogy implies a strictly linear stacking of layers, whereas the spiral model can revisit earlier cycles and overlap activities.
Mapping 3 conflates engineering and evaluation into a single description, which may blur the distinct testing phase of the spiral model.
result.rationale: Most mappings align closely with the intended phases of the spiral model; only the risk‑analysis correspondence requires a modest logical leap. The overall correspondence is therefore judged as well‑aligned, justifying a score of 2 with high confidence.
